Esther sat cross-legged on the sofa in Accra while her flatmate Ada made tea. "Say it aloud," Ada said. "What is the worst that happens if you report the false expense claims?"

"They freeze me out," Esther said slowly. "My manager gives me a bad review. Lunch alone. Someone whispers that I am not a team player."

"Then what?"

"Then I keep copies of my own appraisals and targets, in my own folder. I save the HR contact's number. And I keep three months of salary untouched, just in case." She wrote the list down.

"Do you still want to report it?"

Esther exhaled. "Yes. But now I know what to do if it goes badly."

qa.q: What did Esther plan to keep in her own folder?
qa.a: Copies of her own appraisals and targets.

qa.q: How does Esther feel when she says the worst might be a freeze-out and lunch alone?
qa.a: Esther feels anxious and a little sad about being isolated, but naming it lets her face it without panic.

qa.q: What else could Esther add to her plan, and why?
qa.a: Esther could name one trusted colleague or friend to check in during the hard weeks, because support outside the office makes isolation easier to bear. 🤍

qa.q: How does Ada help Esther see the plan?
qa.a: Ada asks calm questions rather than giving orders, so Esther can find her own answers and feel supported by a flatmate who takes the fear seriously.

grounding: Esther imagines the report going badly and plans with copies of records, an HR contact and savings, so she can act with eyes open.

After everyone left the audit firm's Kolkata office on Thursday, Zainab stayed at her desk with a blank notebook. She had decided to report the vendor payments through the ethics channel. First, though, she wanted to picture it going wrong.
At the top she wrote: 'Six months from now, reporting was a disaster. Why?'
Then she answered herself, slowly. 'My team stops including me. My manager gives me a bad review and says my work slipped. I'm moved to a dull client. I get so anxious I think of quitting, and I can't afford to.'
Under each, she wrote a plan. Save copies of my last two appraisals and clients' thank-you emails from the official system, today. Note the HR partner's name and the ethics office's number. Keep writing down the dates of anything that changes. Check my savings: three months of expenses, just enough.
Vijay, her friend from another team, found her there at eight. 'Still working?'
'Getting ready,' she said. 'Now I know what I'd do if it goes badly.'

qa.q: How many months of expenses does Zainab have in savings?
How does Zainab feel after writing the plan?
qa.a: Steadier and better prepared, still aware it could go badly but no longer afraid of being caught off guard.

qa.q: What else could Zainab add to the plan?
qa.a: A trusted person outside the team to talk to if she feels isolated, like Vijay, and a question to the ethics office about how her identity is protected.

qa.q: How might Vijay see Zainab at her desk at eight?
qa.a: Vijay first thinks she is overworking, then sees she is quietly preparing for something serious.

grounding: Shows an auditor imagining a report going badly and planning for isolation or a bad review with records, HR contacts and savings.

Dear Dilnaz Apa,
I've decided to report what I found at work, through the ethics hotline, on Monday. Before you worry, let me tell you how I've prepared, because I spent the weekend imagining it going badly.
I asked myself: if this turns out terribly, what does 'terribly' look like? My answer: the team goes cold on me, my manager writes a poor review, maybe I'm moved off the good project, and I feel very alone in that office.
So here's my plan for each. I've saved my past appraisals and the client emails praising my work, from the company system, so no one can claim my work slipped. I've noted the HR head's contact and how the hotline's reference process works. I've checked my savings: enough for four months if I had to leave. And I've told you, so I'm not alone with it.
Could we speak every Sunday for a while? That's the last part of the plan.
Your sister,
Ayesha

qa.q: When is Ayesha reporting through the ethics hotline?
What might Ayesha be afraid of?
qa.a: Isolation, a poor review and losing the good project, and feeling very alone in the office.

qa.q: Why is asking for Sunday calls part of a good plan?
qa.a: Regular support from someone outside work helps with loneliness if the team turns cold.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz Apa feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Worried for her sister but reassured by the careful plan, and glad to be asked to help. 🤍

grounding: Shows an employee imagining how reporting could go badly and preparing appraisal records, HR contacts, savings and family support.
